script_text: The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the Son of David, the Son of Abraham: Abraham begot Isaac, Isaac begot Jacob, and Jacob begot Judah and his brothers. Judah begot Perez and Zerah by Tamar, Perez begot Hezron, and Hezron begot Ram. Ram begot Amminadab, Amminadab begot Nahshon, and Nahshon begot Salmon. Salmon begot Boaz by Rahab, Boaz begot Obed by Ruth, Obed begot Jesse, and Jesse begot David the king. David the king begot Solomon by her who had been the wife of Uriah. Solomon begot Rehoboam, Rehoboam begot Abijah, and Abijah begot Asa. Asa begot Jehoshaphat, Jehoshaphat begot Joram, and Joram begot Uzziah. Uzziah begot Jotham, Jotham begot Ahaz, and Ahaz begot Hezekiah. Hezekiah begot Manasseh, Manasseh begot Amon, and Amon begot Josiah. Josiah begot Jeconiah and his brothers about the time they were carried away to Babylon. And after they were brought to Babylon, Jeconiah begot Shealtiel, and Shealtiel begot Zerubbabel.
style_suffix: The illustration style features a warm, earthy palette dominated by muted browns, deep greens, and soft golds, evoking a sense of antiquity and warmth. Lighting is natural and diffused, mimicking the soft glow of oil lamps and candles, with daylight filtering through wooden structures, creating gentle shadows that enhance the three-dimensionality of the scenes. The brush and texture style is rich and tactile, resembling traditional oil painting techniques that emphasize the organic qualities of materials like stone, wood, and fabric, giving depth and life to each element. The camera mood is immersive and inviting, capturing scenes from a slightly elevated perspective to provide a comprehensive view of bustling marketplaces, serene courtyards, or majestic temples, inviting the viewer to step into the past. Care is taken to avoid any modern elements, ensuring that each illustration is a faithful representation of the era, with no contemporary technology or anachronistic details that could disrupt the historical authenticity. Horizontal 16:9 landscape, no text, no watermark, no logos, no book-with-text compositions.
